texts: doha about a lover gone mad for God, dancing before a temple with his shadow
People point at me in the lane and laugh, but I dance alone with my own shadow before the temple, drunk on the Beloved and past caring what anyone says. Please write a doha for such a madman of love.
Let the village laugh; I dance with my shadow before the temple, intoxicated, for the Beloved has stolen my sense.
My neighbors whisper that I have lost my mind, because every evening I sing loudly at the temple steps with my shadow stretching long, and I honestly don't care.
mad dancer, shadow, temple
I wrapped myself in rough cotton and wandered up the mountain singing the Beloved's name while the whole town called me crazy, and I laughed at their words; write a doha about that divine madness.
Rough cotton on my back and the mountain beneath my feet, I am mad, and the Beloved's name is my wine.
doha with cotton and a mountain, a man mad for God's love
My brother quit his job, wore plain cotton and walked up the mountain singing, and when family said he was mad he just grinned.
cotton, mountain, mad lover
They call me drunk and mad; I am, with the Beloved, who poured me a cup of milk and made the world a dream.
doha about a man mad for God who pours milk and ignores everyone's talk
They say I am drunk, and so I am, intoxicated on the Beloved so completely that I would sell all I own for a cup of milk to pour at His feet; compose a doha on this wild devotion.
My uncle gave away his land and now spends every morning pouring milk for the Lord and humming, and nobody in the village knows what to make of him.
mad with milk offering
mad with devotion
doha for a lover mad for the Lord who ignores what the world says
Let them call me mad; I have forgotten my name, my caste and my shame, and my only sanity is the Beloved.
I have lost all sense of shame and caution, dancing in the street with my hair loose, mad for the Beloved while the neighbors tut and stare; please write a doha for the madness of such a lover.
My aunt dances in the lane whenever she hears the Lord's name, her hair loose, and she says the people who laugh are the ones who are truly lost.
singing at the crossroads
doha with a crossroads, a lover mad with divine love, ignoring the crowd
There is a man who sings at the crossroads every dawn, drunk on devotion, and the whole neighborhood has stopped trying to make him sensible.
At the crossroads I stood singing in front of everyone, utterly drunk on the Beloved, and the crowd gathered and mocked, but I heard nothing; compose a doha about this blessed madness.
At the crossroads I sing, and the whole world laughs, and I am too drunk on Him to turn my head.
doha with a mirror and a shadow, a lover mad for the Beloved and happy
When I saw my shadow in the mirror I laughed and danced, I no longer cared who I seemed to be, mad as I am for the Beloved; write a doha on that gladly careless lover.
mirror, shadow, madness
I danced in front of the mirror in my room and saw my shadow dancing too, and I thought how mad I look, and how glad.
In the mirror I saw a madman, in the shadow a dancer, and neither cared what the world thought of the Beloved's.
The world calls it sense, I call it sleep; I woke in the Beloved's intoxication and cannot walk straight again.
drunk on the Beloved
My cousin has been walking around grinning for weeks like he has had too much to drink, and he says he is just in love with God.
a doha about the glorious madness of a lover who doesn't care what people think

Intoxicated with the Beloved I have left all sense behind and walk about like a drunkard, careless of how anyone judges me; please write a doha capturing that glorious, unashamed craziness of the lover.
doha with a beggar and a mirror, a lover mad for the Beloved and proud of it
The beggar and the mirror laugh together; I am the madman who traded all sense for one glance of the Beloved.
The beggar stands before the mirror and sees a king, and I stand before it and see a madman happy beyond reason, intoxicated with the Beloved; compose a doha about being mad in this way.
A beggar by the road looked into a mirror, laughed out loud and then shouted that he was drunk on God, and the crowd thought he was mad.
beggar, mirror, madman
careless lover
I do not care what anyone says about me anymore, I only know that the Beloved has made me wild, and my life is a happy folly; please write me a doha about lovers who are mad with devotion.
My friends think I have lost my mind since I started singing in the morning and giving my stuff away, but I have never felt saner.
doha about the madness of someone in love with God who ignores everyone
Call me a fool, call me mad, I have no ears for the world since the Beloved intoxicated me.
doha about a mad lover planting a seed at the cremation ground
Planting a seed by the cremation ground I laughed, mad with the Beloved, knowing that all of life is a game and he who is drunk on the Lord needs fear nothing; write a long doha for me.
seed, cremation ground, madman
The village madman sits at the cremation ground planting seeds and laughing, and the old people say he is the sanest of us all.
A seed in the cremation ground, a laugh on the lips, the madman plants his joy where others bury their dead.
I sit inside the cage of society's opinion, yet my heart burns with the fire of madness for the Beloved, and I will break out and dance while they watch; compose a doha about such wild love.
doha with a fire and a cage, a lover mad for God breaking free
fire and cage, mad lover
The cage of the world is shut but the fire inside breaks the bars; the madman dances out into the Lord's arms.
My family kept me in a cage of expectations but the fire of devotion got me out, and now I sing in the streets and they have stopped asking me to stop.
beads and cotton, discarded
I have lost the sense to count prayer beads and lost the shame to wear my cotton clean, because the Beloved made me wild; write a doha about how madness replaces the careful rituals of the proper.
I threw down my prayer beads and tore my cotton shawl; the Beloved's madness has made a ritual of my laughter.
My aunt counted her prayer beads for forty years in plain cotton, and then one day she threw them aside and started dancing, and nobody could stop her.
doha with prayer beads and cotton, a person mad for God and careless
jaggery and madness
doha with jaggery, a lover mad and drunk on divine sweetness
Jaggery is sweet, but the Beloved's wine is sweeter; I wander through the lanes mumbling nonsense, entirely mad.
Honey has no taste next to the madness of the Beloved's sweetness, and I wander about intoxicated with it, jaggery in my pocket and nonsense in my mouth; compose a doha on that wild bliss.
He eats jaggery all day and mumbles songs about God in the lanes, and the children call him mad and follow him anyway.
doha with a bitter gourd and a sword, a lover gone mad with the divine
A bitter gourd in my left, a sword in my right, I march mad into the world, for the Beloved has made me fearless.
Like a madman holding a bitter gourd in one hand and a sword in the other, I march into the lanes singing, and nobody dares stop me for I am mad with the Beloved; write a doha for me.
Our local madman walks about with a bitter gourd and an old sword singing devotional songs, and no one dares tease him.
bitter gourd, sword, madman
The snake coils, the bitter gourd stings the mouth, and the madman smiles, for the Beloved is everywhere.
A man in our village sat calmly next to a snake and ate a bitter gourd, saying he was too drunk on God to be afraid, and everyone called him crazy.
snake, bitter gourd, madman
They said I was mad to sit with the snake and drink the bitter gourd juice, but the Beloved has taken my fear and my sense away, and I smile; write a doha on this fearless, careless love.
doha with a snake and a bitter gourd, a lover mad for God and fearless
The musk deer runs mad for the scent, the singer plays his one-string lute; both of us are mad for the Beloved.
I play a one-string lute and run through the fields like a musk deer, and my friends say I have lost my mind, but I smile.
musk deer, one-string lute
doha with a musk deer and a one-string lute, a wild lover of the Beloved
The musk deer runs mad through the wild after the scent he carries, and I wander drunk with the one-string lute in my hand, mad for the Beloved; please compose a doha for this.
He left his house and his shop and now sits under the neem singing all day, drunk on God, and people say he has lost his mind.
I left the house, my name and my wealth; the madman of the Beloved needs no roof but His smile.
I left my house, my wife, my work, all to wander the streets singing for the Beloved, and they call me mad and turn their backs on me; compose a doha for the lover who ignores everyone.
doha about a man who left his house in madness for the Beloved
leaving the house, mad
My grandmother's loom-woven shawl flew behind her as she danced barefoot across the sand, singing out loud, and the village called her mad.
sand and loom shawl, madness
Barefoot on hot sand, my loom-woven shawl torn, I am mad, and the sky itself is my audience.
Walking on hot sand, with a loom-woven shawl flung over one shoulder, I shouted the Beloved's name to the sky, careless of all, and everyone said I was mad; please write a doha for me.
doha with sand and a loom, someone mad for the Beloved
I have no wish to be sensible, no desire to be careful, I want only to be mad for the Beloved and dance in the street like a fool and a lover, so write me a doha.
can u do a doha about a lover who is mad and happy about being mad
Let the sensible have their sense; I have the Beloved's madness and a heart that dances without a reason.
choosing madness
I've stopped caring about being proper, I just want to be silly and wild for what I love, and be called a fool for it.
They offered me milk and warned me of the snake, but I was too drunk on the Beloved to be afraid and laughed as I drank, a madman among the sane; compose a doha about this fearless madness.
milk and snake, fearless madness
A village madman once fed milk to a snake and sang to it, and while everyone ran he was just laughing, drunk on God.
doha with milk and a snake, a lover mad for God and not afraid
The snake bows to the madman and the milk turns to nectar, for he is drunk on the Beloved and fears nothing.
The beggar at the gate sings out the Beloved's name, utterly mad, and the passers-by cover their ears, but he does not care, for he is drunk on a wine no tavern sells; write a long doha for me.
the mad beggar
Our local beggar is happier than any of us, he sings all day, mumbles God's name and nobody can say if he's mad or holy.
doha about a beggar who is mad with divine love and ignores the crowd
The beggar sings, the people cover their ears, and he is drunk on a wine that no tavern has ever poured.
Shame fell first, then fame, and then the self; what remains is a madman and the Beloved.
doha for a lover mad for God, dropping shame and status
My college friend left everything for his path and he now laughs at everything we thought was important, like a person drunk in the morning.
madness of love
Please write a doha about the madness of someone so lost in love for God that they no longer care for fame, wealth, status or shame, and who dance without any embarrassment at all.
The bee loves the flower so mad that it forgets its way home, and my tongue is so mad with the Beloved's name that it cannot stop; compose a doha about that wild, drunken love.
bee, tongue, madness
doha with a bee and a restless tongue, a lover mad for the Beloved
The bee forgets the hive in the flower; my tongue forgets the world in the Beloved's name; both of us are mad.
My grandmother chants the name nonstop, her tongue never still, and hums like a bee, and the family has given up trying to quiet her.
doha about whirling in a mosque courtyard, mad for the Beloved
whirling at the mosque
They stare at the whirling madman in the mosque; he sees only the Beloved and spins as the world falls away.
In the mosque courtyard they stared as I whirled and laughed, but I was drunk and past all caring, mad with the Beloved, and let them think what they would; please write a doha on this blessed state.
A stranger started whirling in the courtyard of the mosque last Friday, arms open, laughing, and no one dared stop him.
My brother has been called a fool by half the village for the way he loves, but he is the happiest man I know.
The world mocks and the madman laughs, for what is mockery to one who has swallowed the Beloved?
doha about being a mad lover who is happy and doesn't mind mockery
Tell me in a doha how a lover gone mad with the Beloved no longer minds if the whole world mocks him, and how he is the happiest man alive despite everyone calling him a fool.
happy fool of love
A snake round his neck and a song on his lips, the madman is too drunk on the Beloved to feel fear.
The snake wrapped round his neck did not frighten the madman, for he was so full of the Beloved that he felt nothing, and the crowd ran off screaming; write a long doha of that careless intoxication.
A mad faqir came to our village with a snake around his neck singing love songs for God, and the children followed in awe.
doha with a snake around the neck of a lover mad with divine love
madman with a snake
doha with a door, a mad lover who knocks all night for the Beloved
I knock at the door in the night, mad, shameless, and the neighbors curse me, but the Beloved has stolen my sense.
Banging on the door of the Beloved in the middle of the night, I was called mad by the neighbors, but I banged again, drunk and shameless, till dawn; compose a doha about the lover who will not stop.
At midnight my son stood banging on the door shouting a bhajan, drunk on devotion, and the whole street opened their windows.
knocking at the door
doha about a mad lover who gives everything and doesn't care what people say
spinning, giving, mad
Spinning like a drunkard under the open sky, I gave away everything I owned, singing and laughing, and not one thing the world said touched me; please write a doha for the lover mad for the Beloved.
My uncle gave all his savings to a stranger, then spun around laughing, and the family thought he'd gone mad.
I gave away everything and spun until I fell; the world's opinion blew away, the Beloved's intoxication remained.
short doha about being crazy in love with God and not caring who sees
My mum says I used to be so careful about what people think, but now I'm a mad person singing out loud and she's weirdly proud.
I do not understand what they mean by shame; all I know is that when I think of the Beloved I laugh and cry and dance, and they call me mad for it, so write me a doha for that.
Shame and sense have both departed; the Beloved has settled in and the madman has no complaints.
no shame left
Our village madman talks to God out loud on the road and dances at any occasion, and the elders say he is the only one who is awake.
Mad at the funeral, mad at the wedding, the madman is drunk on a love that is neither gladness nor grief.
village madman
There is a man in our village who talks to the Lord loudly on the road, dances at funerals and laughs at weddings, and everyone calls him mad, but I think he is drunk on the Beloved; write a doha.
doha about the village madman who is drunk on the Beloved
doha with a water well and an ocean, a lover mad with divine love
I stand at the water well, wanting to throw myself into the ocean of the Beloved, mad as I am, drunk and unashamed, and the villagers think I have lost my mind; write a doha for me.
At the water well I shout the Beloved's name; the ocean hears and the madman wades in laughing.
Folks say I'm mad because I sit by the water well singing about the ocean of God, though I have never even seen the ocean.
water well, ocean, madness
The world's good name I have left on the road; I walk bare in the Beloved's madness and I am warm.
I used to care so much what my colleagues think but ever since I started singing hymns on the metro I have never felt freer.
reputation thrown away
short doha for a fool in love with God, past caring for opinion
I stopped worrying about my reputation the day I fell for the Divine, and now I am a happy fool who walks about humming, so please write me a doha about someone mad in love.
The boatman said a madman had been singing on the bridge all night while watching the boat, and by dawn he had given away all his clothes.
doha with a bridge and a boat, a lover mad for the Beloved
bridge and boat, a madman
The bridge is crossed, the boat is left, and the madman wanders singing; he has no destination but the Beloved.

Over the bridge by the boat landing the madman wandered laughing, throwing flowers on the water and calling the Beloved's name, while the boatmen shook their heads; compose a doha for his joyous madness.

He stood at the door and the water well was behind him, and he shouted the Beloved's name until his voice cracked, mad with love, while the neighbors looked on in shock; write me a doha about such unashamed love.
The door is open and the madman shouts, the water well echoes, and the Beloved hears him from every direction.
door, water well, mad cry
A man stood by the door of the village water well, shouting for the Lord for two days, and some said mad and others said blessed.
doha with a door and a water well, a mad shout for the Beloved
Torn cotton on my back and a song on my lips, I am the fool of the fair, and the Beloved is my king.
My uncle wore the same torn cotton shirt for weeks and sang at the fair, saying that love of God made all clothes pointless.
torn cotton, happy fool
I wore torn cotton and sang the Beloved's praises at the fair, drunk and happy, and people laughed, but I only laughed with them; compose a doha for the free-hearted madness of the lover.
doha with torn cotton, a happy fool mad for the Beloved
An arrow pierced the madman's heart at the spinning wheel, and he left his work and ran into the street singing the Beloved's name, wild and happy; write a long doha about the lover's madness.
doha with an arrow and a spinning wheel, a man gone mad for the Lord
My grandfather felt an arrow of devotion strike him at the spinning wheel one morning, and he has been singing hymns at the roadside for years.
The arrow struck at the spinning wheel, the weaver ran into the street, and the world never saw him sane again.
arrow and spinning wheel, madman
chat style doha, drunk on the Beloved, crazy and proud
Lost in the Beloved I can no longer tell night from day, speech from song, or sense from folly, and so the world calls me a madman; please write a doha that sings of this beautiful confusion.
Night and day, sense and folly all run together in the madman who is drunk on the Beloved.
I've been walking around in a daze since I started going to satsang, laughing at nothing, and my friends say I have gone a bit loopy.
confused with love
the lion and the madman
Everyone says my uncle must be mad because he stood in front of a lion at the zoo and began to sing, saying he was too drunk on God to be scared.
doha with a lion, a lover mad with divine love and past fear
The lion roars and the madman laughs; the Beloved has swallowed his fear and left him only a song.
Fear left me when I fell mad for the Beloved, and now I would sit unmoved in front of a lion, so intoxicated am I; write me a doha on this reckless, wonderful madness.
The beggar sits on a stone and laughs at coins and curses alike; he is mad, and the Beloved's wine is his only meal.
doha with a beggar and a stone, a man mad and drunk for the divine
A beggar sits by a stone, drunk on the Beloved, and people throw coins and abuse alike, but he gives them all back with a laugh, and the world calls him mad; compose a doha about such a lover.
There is a beggar who sits on a stone outside our school, throws every coin back, and babbles about the Beloved, and the kids think he's crazy.
beggar on a stone
Mad to the sane, sane to the mad; the lover laughs, for he knows which world is the dream.
who is the madman?
Write me a doha for a person who is so intoxicated with their love for God that they have given up trying to make sense, and who laughs when others call them mad, knowing the joke is on the world.
My grandfather laughed when the whole family said he had gone mad, and said it was the first time he had ever felt awake.
doha about someone who is happily mad for God and laughs at their critics
Is it crazy to love someone so much that you forget to care about what the world thinks of you? Please compose a doha that celebrates that sweet and shameless madness of a lover in the mood.
mad and unashamed
If it is madness, let me be mad, for the sane have never known what the Beloved gives.
My friends tease me that I'm crazy because I sing aloud and give my money away, but I've never been happier in my life.
doha about being a little crazy in love and not caring who knows
doha with a traveler dancing at a cremation ground, mad with God's love
At the cremation ground a traveler dances, and the mourners stare; he is mad with the Beloved, and the grave is a stage.
A traveler passing the cremation ground started to dance and sing hymns, and the mourners were scandalized, but the old women smiled.
traveler dancing, cremation ground
At the cremation ground a traveler laughed and danced, mad with the Beloved, because death had no sting for one who was drunk on the Lord; write a doha about his strange gladness.
The lion looks at the madman and bows his head, for the Beloved looks out of both their eyes.
My uncle bowed to a lion in the circus, saying he saw the Lord in its eyes, and the whole crowd thought he had lost his mind.
doha with a lion and a madman who sees the Beloved in everything
The lion behind the bars stares at the madman who walks up and bows to him, so drunk on the Beloved that he sees the Beloved in everything; compose a doha about this fearless madness.
bowing to the lion
losing all caution
I let go of my good name; the madman keeps no accounts, for the Beloved has paid every debt.
doha about a lover who lost all caution, mad for God
Mad for the Beloved I have given away my sleep, my good name, and my caution, and laugh at all those who still keep accounts; please write a doha for a lover who has become gloriously careless.
I used to keep careful accounts of everything, now I give away whatever I have and sing at night, and everyone calls me mad.
People say I am mad because I spend hours watching the swan on the lake and singing, but I feel more alive than I ever did.
doha with a swan, a drifting lover mad for the Beloved
The swan floats on the lake, ignorant of the crowd, and so do I wander, drunk on the Beloved and past caring what anyone says; compose a doha on a lover in a state of divine madness.
swan, mad drift
The swan sails on, the world stares, and the madman drifts after the Beloved, beyond the reach of opinion.
My cousin is a pearl diver and is mad about the deep water, and he says that is how he feels about God, willing to drown happily.
The pearl diver plunged into the deep, mad with the hunt, and I too have plunged into the Beloved, losing my sense; write a long doha about the madness of the one who seeks a single pearl.
pearl and madness
doha with a pearl, a mad lover who dives into the Beloved
The pearl-diver risks his life for one pearl; the madman risks his name for the Beloved, and thinks it cheap.
My family called a doctor because I wouldn't stop singing about God at night, but I felt more sane than I ever have.
They shut me in my room and called the doctor, as I would not stop singing for the Beloved, but I only sang louder, mad and joyful; write me a doha about the stubborn madness of love.
They tried to cure me, but the madman sang louder, for the Beloved had already taken his reason.
doha about being called crazy for loving God and loving it
they called me mad
The cleric and the boatman both thought I was mad when I sang in the boat at dawn, drunk on the Beloved, but I laughed, because I had found what they were still looking for; compose a doha.
doha with a cleric and a boat, a lover mad for God and singing
A cleric on the ferry boat frowned at me for singing, and the boatman smiled, and I thought: what a joyous madness it is.
cleric, boat, mad singer
The cleric frowns, the boatman stares, and the madman sings in the boat, for he has drunk what neither has found.
Mad, mad, mad for the Beloved, unashamed, unreasonable and happy, I want a long doha that celebrates a lover who has thrown away every rule of the world and lives free, wild with a single name.
I have thrown away every rule and burned every excuse; I am a madman, and the Beloved's name is all my sense.
totally mad
doha about a lover gone mad and loving it
My friend became so mad for God that he gave up his phone, his office and all his plans, and he says he has never been happier.
doha with a bee drunk on nectar, a lover drunk on the Beloved
The bee staggers drunk from flower to flower, and the madman staggers drunk through the world after the Beloved.
A bee drunk on nectar blunders about the garden and doesn't care what the flowers think, and I blunder about the world mad for the Beloved; write a doha about intoxicated love, please.
a drunken bee
I watched a bee stumble drunk through the flowers and thought of my uncle who stumbles through life just as happily, mad for God.
